title: The Market Day Town (Ka Shnong Ba-Iew)
cultural_context: Vivid phawar depicting the eight-day market cycle (Iewduh, Iewbah, Iewrynghep) of the Khasi hills, from 'Ka Phawar-rwai Khasi' (1973).
lyrics_khasi:
Hoi-kiw! Wan sha ka iew,
Ha ka sngi ba la buh,
Ki tymmen ki samla
Ki kiew na man ki shnong;
Ki kit khoh, ki kit shang,
Ki wan die kwai bad tympew,
U sohkymphor, u sohphlang,
Bad u sohpetbeng ba thiang.

Ka iew ka sawa kynjai,
Ki ktien kmen ki pait,
Hangne ki paralok
Ki ia shem bad ia dait;
Ka iew u Khasi
Kam dei tang ka nong,
Hynrei ka kynhun
Ba pyniatylli ia ka ri.
lyrics_english:
Hoi-kiw! Come to the marketplace,
Upon the designated market day,
Elders and youths alike
Ascend from every hillside hamlet;
Carrying woven conical baskets (Khoh),
Selling betel nut and fresh pan leaf,
Mountain apples, edible crisp tubers,
And luscious wild berries.

The bazaar hums with spirited life,
Laughter and greetings ring out,
Here long-parted friends
Meet and share betel quid;
The Khasi traditional market
Is more than mere trade,
It is the living bond
That unites the entire motherland.
